provenance.note: Assembled August 2026. PM&DC publishes the curriculum but no reusable past papers for recent cycles, so this bank is original practice questions written strictly to the PM&DC Uniform Curriculum (final, May 2025) topic lists, replicating the official 180-MCQ distribution (Biology 81, Chemistry 45, Physics 36, English 9, Logical Reasoning 9) over the full 180 minutes. Every question is labeled practice. Not affiliated with PM&DC.

marking.note: 180 MCQs, 180 marks, no negative marking (PM&DC MDCAT pattern).

questions.stem: Which organelle is the main site of aerobic respiration and of ATP synthesis in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion carries out the Krebs cycle and electron transport on its matrix and inner membrane, so it supplies most of the cell's ATP. Ribosomes make protein, the Golgi packages it and lysosomes digest material.

questions.stem: Enzymes speed up biological reactions mainly because they
options: make an endergonic reaction become exergonic
supply the substrate with extra kinetic energy
increase the activation energy of the reverse reaction only
lower the activation energy that reacting molecules must acquire
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative route of lower activation energy; it does not alter the free-energy change of the reaction and is not used up.

questions.stem: Modification, concentration, packaging and dispatch of proteins for secretion or for lysosomes is the main function of the
questions.explanation: The Golgi cisternae receive transport vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum, modify the proteins (for example by adding carbohydrate) and pin off secretory vesicles.

questions.stem: In the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane, the word mosaic refers mainly to
options: the two phospholipid layers arranged tail to tail
the irregular pattern of protein molecules embedded in and attached to the lipid bilayer
the cholesterol molecules lying between the hydrocarbon tails
the carbohydrate chains present only on the outer surface
questions.explanation: Integral and peripheral proteins of many shapes and sizes are scattered through the bilayer like pieces of a mosaic, while the lipids and most proteins drift laterally (fluid).

questions.stem: A leaf epidermal cell is placed in concentrated sodium chloride solution and its protoplast shrinks away from the wall. The correct explanation is that
options: water leaves the cell by osmosis, the vacuole shrinks and the plasma membrane pulls away from the rigid wall
salt enters the cell and dissolves the cellulose wall
the cell wall contracts as its turgor pressure falls to zero
the cytoplasm sets into a solid gel in the strong salt solution
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic medium the cell loses water and plasmolyses. The fully permeable, inelastic wall keeps its shape, so it is the protoplast that shrinks.

questions.stem: Which process moves dissolved substances across a membrane against their concentration gradient?
options: Osmosis through a partially permeable membrane
Active transport coupled to ATP hydrolysis
Facilitated diffusion through a channel protein
questions.explanation: Only active transport uses metabolic energy (usually ATP) to pump solutes uphill; diffusion, osmosis and filtration are all downhill and passive.

questions.stem: Which lipid is the principal structural component of every cell membrane?
questions.explanation: Amphipathic phospholipids form the continuous bilayer that is the framework of all membranes; cholesterol is inserted between the tails in animal membranes but triglycerides, waxes and steroids do not form bilayers.

questions.stem: The activity of an enzyme falls sharply when the temperature is raised well above its optimum because
options: the substrate molecules are destroyed by the heat
the enzyme is converted into a different protein
the active site is permanently blocked by the product
hydrogen bonds and other weak bonds of the tertiary structure break, so the active site loses its shape
questions.explanation: Heat breaks the weak bonds that hold the enzyme's three-dimensional shape; the active site is distorted, substrate no longer fits and the enzyme is denatured.

questions.stem: During which phase of mitosis do the centromeres divide and the sister chromatids move towards opposite poles?
questions.explanation: Anaphase is the moving-apart stage; in metaphase the chromosomes are aligned at the equator and in telophase the nuclear envelopes re-form.

questions.stem: After a cell is damaged or dies, its own proteins and organelles are digested by hydrolytic enzymes released from the
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases; their rupture brings about autolysis, and they also digest material taken in by phagocytosis or by autophagy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is found in a bacterial cell but not in a human white blood cell?
options: Circular DNA lying free in a nucleoid region
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes have no nuclear envelope, their genome being a naked circular molecule in a nucleoid. Both cell types do possess a membrane, cytoplasm and ribosomes (70S in bacteria, 80S in humans).

questions.stem: For each molecule of ATP hydrolysed, the sodium-potassium pump of a nerve cell membrane transfers
options: 3 sodium ions out of the axoplasm and 2 potassium ions into it
2 sodium ions out and 3 potassium ions in
3 sodium ions in and 2 potassium ions out
1 sodium ion out in exchange for 1 potassium ion in
questions.explanation: The Na+/K+-ATPase is electrogenic: 3 Na+ are pumped out for every 2 K+ taken in, using one ATP, which helps maintain the resting potential.

questions.stem: Which pair of organelles provides the strongest support for the endosymbiotic theory?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own circular DNA, their own 70S-type ribosomes, double membranes and divide independently, all signs of free-living ancestors.

questions.stem: A cell of the adrenal cortex that is specialised for synthesising steroid hormones would be expected to contain an especially abundant
options: rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes
population of free ribosomes in polysomes
questions.explanation: The enzymes that build steroid (lipid) molecules are membrane-bound enzymes of the smooth ER, so steroid-secreting cells of the adrenal cortex and the testis are rich in it.

questions.stem: Which nitrogenous base occurs in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA replaces thymine with uracil, which pairs with adenine; adenine, guanine and cytosine are common to both nucleic acids.

questions.stem: A competitive inhibitor reduces the velocity of an enzyme-catalysed reaction because it
options: binds to the substrate molecule and prevents it reaching the enzyme
binds to a site other than the active site and changes the enzyme's shape
hydrolyses the enzyme at very low inhibitor concentration
occupies the active site, so its effect can be overcome by raising the substrate concentration
questions.explanation: A competitive inhibitor is usually substrate-like and reversibly blocks the active site; enough substrate out-competes it, so Vmax is still reached and only Km rises.

questions.stem: The carbohydrate chains of glycoproteins and glycolipids on the outer face of the plasma membrane function mainly in
options: forming the permeability barrier of the membrane
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx acts as an identification system, as in antigens of the ABO and tissue types and as receptors for hormones; the barrier function belongs to the bilayer itself.

questions.stem: Which pair of substances is built entirely from amino-acid units?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin and insulin are both proteins, so their monomers are amino acids. Glycogen and cellulose are polysaccharides of glucose, the steroids are lipids and the nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides.

questions.stem: A food sample gives a blue-black colour with iodine solution, stays blue with Benedict's reagent on heating, and turns violet with Biuret reagent. The sample contains
questions.explanation: Iodine blue-black proves starch and Biuret violet proves protein, while the unchanged blue of Benedict's shows no reducing sugar is present.

questions.stem: Replication of DNA takes place during which stage of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: Synthesis phase of interphase is when each chromosome is duplicated into two chromatids; G1 and G2 are growth gaps and in prophase the chromosomes merely condense.

questions.stem: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair takes place during
questions.explanation: Chiasmata form when homologues synapse in prophase I and exchange segments; meiosis II and mitosis involve no pairing of homologues.

questions.stem: The final result of meiosis in a germ cell is
questions.explanation: One replication is followed by two divisions, so a diploid cell yields four genetically different haploid cells (sperm, or one ovum plus polar bodies).

questions.stem: The semi-conservative replication of DNA was demonstrated by the density-labelling experiment using heavy nitrogen (15N) performed by
questions.explanation: Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in 15N then transferred it to 14N and followed the hybrid bands of DNA in a caesium chloride gradient. Hershey and Chase proved DNA is the genetic material of a phage.

questions.stem: There are 64 possible codons but only 20 amino acids. How many codons specify amino acids?
questions.explanation: Three codons (UAA, UAG and UGA) are stop signals that code for no amino acid, leaving 61 sense codons; the code is degenerate because several codons share one amino acid.

questions.stem: The enzyme that synthesises messenger RNA using a DNA template is
questions.explanation: During transcription, RNA polymerase reads the template strand and builds a complementary RNA chain. Reverse transcriptase (RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) works the other way in retroviruses.

questions.stem: A test cross, used to find the genotype of an organism showing a dominant phenotype, is a mating with
options: another individual with the same phenotype
questions.explanation: Only a homozygous recessive partner reveals hidden recessive alleles: a dominant parent gives all dominant offspring if homozygous but a 1:1 ratio if heterozygous.

questions.stem: The phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a Mendelian monohybrid cross with complete dominance is
questions.explanation: F1 heterozygotes selfed give 3 dominant to 1 recessive in phenotype but 1:2:1 in genotype. A 9:3:3:1 ratio belongs to a dihybrid cross.

questions.stem: A man with X-linked red-green colour blindness marries a woman with normal vision who is homozygous for the normal allele. Which statement about their children is correct?
options: All their sons will be colour-blind
All their daughters will be carriers with normal vision and all their sons will have normal vision
Half their daughters will be colour-blind
None of their children can carry the colour-blindness allele
questions.explanation: The father passes his affected X to every daughter, making them XN Xc carriers with normal vision, and his Y to his sons, who receive a normal X from their mother. Daughters can, however, pass the allele on.

questions.stem: Analysis of the DNA of a bacterium shows that adenine makes up 30 per cent of its bases. What percentage of the bases is guanine?
questions.explanation: By Chargaff's rule A = T = 30 per cent each, so the remaining 40 per cent is G + C and G = C = 20 per cent.

questions.stem: The reduction of the chromosome number to half takes place at
questions.explanation: At anaphase I whole homologues separate while their sister chromatids remain joined, so the nuclei produced after meiosis I are already haploid.

questions.stem: Sickle-cell haemoglobin differs from normal haemoglobin because valine replaces glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta chain. The underlying mutation is a
options: substitution of a single base pair in the coding region of the globin gene
loss of one chromosome during meiosis
fusion of two chromosomes at the centromere
questions.explanation: A gene (point) mutation changes the codon GAG to GUG in the beta-globin DNA, so the messenger RNA specifies valine; neither the number nor the general structure of the chromosomes changes.

questions.stem: The forelimbs of a whale, a bat and a human contain the same basic arrangement of bones yet are used for swimming, flying and grasping. They are
options: acquired characters passed on to the next generation
questions.explanation: Same structure, different function and a common ancestor define homology and divergent evolution; analogous organs such as the wing of a bird and the wing of an insect have different structure but similar function.

questions.stem: In a large population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium the frequency of a recessive allele q is 0.2. What is the expected frequency of heterozygous individuals?
questions.explanation: With p = 0.8 and q = 0.2 the heterozygote frequency is 2pq = 2 x 0.8 x 0.2 = 0.32. The 0.04 value is q squared, the homozygous recessives.

questions.stem: In chromatin the DNA double helix is coiled around a core of eight histone molecules; this repeating packing unit is the
questions.explanation: The nucleosome is the basic unit of DNA packing, with linker DNA running from one histone core to the next.

questions.stem: The initiator codon on messenger RNA is 5'-AUG-3'. The anticodon of the transfer RNA that carries methionine is
questions.explanation: Codon and anticodon are complementary and antiparallel and RNA uses uracil, so UAC pairs with AUG. TAC is the DNA triplet of the template strand, which is the usual trap.

questions.stem: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. Which blood groups can their children have?
options: Group A or group B only
Any of the four ABO groups
questions.explanation: The father gives either I(A) or I(B) and the mother always gives i, so the children are I(A)i (group A) or I(B)i (group B); groups AB and O cannot appear.

questions.stem: Non-disjunction of the sex chromosomes can produce a child with the karyotype 47, XXY. This individual is male and shows
questions.explanation: An extra X in a male gives Klinefelter syndrome with small testes and usually sterility; Turner syndrome is the 45, X0 female and Down syndrome is trisomy of chromosome 21.

questions.stem: In industrial areas of England the dark melanic form of the peppered moth Biston betularia replaced the pale form on soot-blackened tree trunks. This is an example of
options: stabilising selection that keeps the intermediate form
directional selection favouring one extreme of the variation
questions.explanation: Birds removed the conspicuous pale moths, so survival favoured one extreme and the gene pool shifted toward the dark form.

questions.stem: Albinism is an autosomal recessive condition. Two normally pigmented heterozygous parents have three children. What is the probability that all three children are albino?
questions.explanation: Each birth independently has a 1/4 chance of being aa, so three affected children have probability (1/4) cubed = 1/64.

questions.stem: The two genes A/a and B/b assort independently. In the progeny of the cross AaBb x AaBb, what proportion are heterozygous for both genes?
questions.explanation: Aa x Aa gives 1/2 Aa and Bb x Bb gives 1/2 Bb, so by the product rule 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4 of the offspring are AaBb. The 9/16 value is the double-dominant phenotype.

questions.stem: Which structure normally acts as the pacemaker of the human heart?
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node in the wall of the right atrium fires spontaneously about 70 times a minute and the wave of excitation then passes to the AV node; the AV node can pace only as a slower back-up.

questions.stem: Oxygenated blood is conveyed from the lungs to the left atrium by the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins are the only veins carrying oxygen-rich blood; the pulmonary artery takes deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which formed element of blood initiates clotting by adhering to damaged endothelium and aggregating at a wound?
questions.explanation: Platelets, fragments of megakaryocytes, form the temporary plug and release thromboplastin that starts the cascade converting prothrombin into thrombin.

questions.stem: The guard valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle is the
options: semilunar valve of the pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: The left auriculo-ventricular aperture has two cusps and is called bicuspid or mitral; the tricuspid valve guards the right aperture and the semilunar valves lie at the roots of the aorta and pulmonary artery.

questions.stem: The wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than that of the right ventricle because the left ventricle
options: receives blood from the lungs at high pressure
pumps blood into the low-resistance pulmonary circuit
must generate the high pressure needed to drive blood through the systemic circuit
contains more oxygen than the right ventricle
questions.explanation: The greater muscle mass of the left wall produces the higher systolic pressure needed to push blood around the whole body, whereas the right ventricle only serves the nearby lungs.

questions.stem: If the stroke volume is 70 cm3 and the heart rate is 72 beats per minute, the cardiac output is approximately
questions.explanation: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 70 x 72 = 5040 cm3 per minute, about 5 dm3, the normal resting value.

questions.stem: Most of the oxygen carried in human blood is present as
options: oxygen dissolved freely in the plasma
questions.explanation: Oxygen combines reversibly with the iron of haemoglobin within erythrocytes; only some 2 to 3 per cent is dissolved in plasma.

questions.stem: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood takes place across the thin walls of the
questions.explanation: Alveoli offer a vast moist epithelial surface closely opposed to the pulmonary capillaries; the conducting passages are far too thick for diffusion.

questions.stem: During inspiration in a resting person
options: the diaphragm contracts and flattens, the thoracic volume increases and air rushes in
the diaphragm domes upward and air is expelled
the internal intercostal muscles contract and the ribs move downward
the thoracic volume decreases so the pressure inside rises above atmospheric
questions.explanation: Contraction of the diaphragm and of the external intercostals enlarges the chest cavity, intrapulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric and air flows in.

questions.stem: About seven-tenths of the carbon dioxide transported in the blood is carried as
options: carbon dioxide dissolved in the plasma
carbonic acid inside the red cells
bicarbonate ions dissolved in the plasma
questions.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase of the red cell forms carbonic acid which at once dissociates; the bicarbonate ions diffuse out into plasma with the chloride shift and account for roughly 70 per cent of the CO2 transported.

questions.stem: The breathing rate rises steeply during heavy muscular exercise mainly because
options: the oxygen shortage in the muscles acts directly on the diaphragm
the vagus nerve to the heart is cut off completely at once
rising carbon dioxide and the resulting fall in pH of the cerebrospinal fluid stimulate the respiratory centre of the medulla
the stretch receptors of the lungs inhibit the pneumotaxic centre
questions.explanation: Central chemoreceptors of the medulla are the dominant control: CO2 crosses into the cerebrospinal fluid, forms carbonic acid and the hydrogen ions excite the respiratory centre. Falling oxygen is only a weak stimulus acting through the carotid and aortic bodies.

questions.stem: Bile, which emulsifies fat in the duodenum, is produced by the
questions.explanation: Hepatic cells secrete bile, which is then stored and concentrated in the gall bladder; bile contains bile salts and pigment but no enzyme.

questions.stem: Pepsin of the gastric juice hydrolyses proteins most rapidly at a pH of about
questions.explanation: Pepsin is an acid protease with an optimum near pH 2, maintained by hydrochloric acid; the alkaline pH 8 values suit trypsin in the duodenum.

questions.stem: The products of fat digestion, fatty acids and glycerol, are absorbed from the small intestine chiefly into the
options: epithelial cells of the stomach wall
columnar cells of the gall bladder
questions.explanation: After resynthesis into protein-coated fat droplets in the epithelium, the lipids enter the blind-ended lymphatic lacteal of the villus, whereas glucose and amino acids enter the blood capillaries.

questions.stem: Glucose and amino acids absorbed from the ileum are carried by the blood first to the
options: liver, by the hepatic portal vein
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein drains the gut to the liver, where excess glucose is converted to glycogen and amino acids are deaminated before the blood returns to the heart.

questions.stem: The urea found in mammalian blood plasma is formed mainly by
options: deamination of excess amino acids in liver cells
breakdown of uric acid in the kidney
putrefaction of undigested protein in the colon
hydrolysis of nucleotides in the blood plasma
questions.explanation: Amino acids that cannot be stored are deaminated in the liver; the ammonia is converted to urea by the ornithine cycle and the rest of the molecule is oxidised or turned to glucose.

questions.stem: The structural and functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each nephron carries out ultrafiltration at Bowman's capsule and selective reabsorption along the tubule; a glomerulus is only its capillary knot.

questions.stem: Antidiuretic hormone reduces the volume of urine by making the walls of the distal tubules and collecting ducts
options: more permeable to water, because aquaporin channels are inserted into the tubule cell membranes
able to secrete urea actively into the filtrate
questions.explanation: ADH from the posterior pituitary causes vesicles carrying aquaporin water channels to fuse with the tubule cell membranes, so water is osmotically reabsorbed into the hypertonic medulla.

questions.stem: A desert rodent whose kidneys possess very long loops of Henle and long vasa recta would be expected to
options: excrete its nitrogen mainly as uric acid
produce a large volume of dilute urine
reabsorb almost no water from the filtrate
produce a small volume of very concentrated urine
questions.explanation: A long loop of Henle creates a steeper medullary osmotic gradient, so more water is withdrawn from the collecting duct and little, concentrated urine is passed.

questions.stem: Which hormone lowers the glucose concentration of the blood after a meal?
questions.explanation: Insulin from the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans promotes uptake of glucose by liver, muscle and fat cells and its conversion to glycogen; glucagon, adrenaline and cortisol all raise blood glucose.

questions.stem: When the environmental temperature is high, the human body increases heat loss mainly by
options: vasoconstriction of the arterioles of the skin
vasodilation of the skin capillaries and secretion of sweat
raising the metabolic rate and shivering
contracting the erector muscles of the hairs
questions.explanation: Dilated skin capillaries bring more blood to the surface to radiate and conduct heat, and the evaporation of sweat removes further heat; the other three responses conserve heat in the cold.

questions.stem: In the central nervous system the myelin sheath round an axon is formed by the
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes myelinate central axons, one cell wrapping several fibres, whereas Schwann cells sheath peripheral axons; astrocytes support and microglia phagocytose.

questions.stem: The neurotransmitter released at the motor end-plate of a neuromuscular junction is
questions.explanation: Synaptic vesicles discharge acetylcholine, which depolarises the sarcolemma and is then split by acetylcholinesterase; the others act at different central synapses.

questions.stem: The depolarisation phase of a nerve action potential is caused mainly by
options: efflux of potassium ions through leak channels
active pumping of sodium ions out of the axon
influx of sodium ions through voltage-gated channels
influx of chloride ions into the axon
questions.explanation: When threshold is reached the sodium gates open and Na+ rushes in, reversing the potential to about plus 40 mV; potassium efflux afterwards repolarises the membrane.

questions.stem: The correct sequence of components in a reflex arc is
options: receptor, motor neuron, relay neuron, sensory neuron, effector
effector, sensory neuron, relay neuron, motor neuron, receptor
receptor, motor neuron, spinal cord, sensory neuron, effector
receptor, sensory neuron, relay neuron, motor neuron, effector
questions.explanation: A stimulus is detected by a receptor, passed in on a sensory neurone, integrated by a connector neurone in the spinal cord and carried out by a motor neurone to an effector.

questions.stem: Which hormone lowers the calcium ion concentration of the blood?
options: Calcitonin secreted by the thyroid gland
questions.explanation: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast activity so less calcium leaves bone and the blood level falls; parathyroid hormone is its antagonist and raises blood calcium.

questions.stem: Which hormone brings about the fight-or-flight responses of increased heart rate, bronchodilation and glycogen breakdown?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine) from the adrenal medulla is released during stress and prepares the body for sudden action.

questions.stem: The region of the brain that contains the centres for temperature regulation, hunger and thirst, that controls water balance and that directs the pituitary gland is the
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the homeostatic control centre and links nervous and endocrine systems through the hypophyseal portal system to the pituitary.

questions.stem: Accommodation of the human eye for near vision involves
options: the suspensory ligaments slackening while the ciliary muscles relax
contraction of the ciliary muscles, slackening of the suspensory ligaments and a more convex lens
relaxation of the ciliary muscles with tightening of the ligaments and a flatter lens
contraction of the dilator muscle of the iris
questions.explanation: The ciliary body forms a ring of smooth muscle; when it contracts the ligaments go slack and the elastic lens rounds up, increasing its refracting power for a near object.

questions.stem: In the male reproductive system, sperm complete their maturation and are stored in the
questions.explanation: Sperm produced in the seminiferous tubules pass into the coiled epididymis, where they gain motility and fertilising ability before the vas deferens carries them away.

questions.stem: Ovulation of the secondary oocyte from the mature Graafian follicle is triggered by the mid-cycle surge of
questions.explanation: Rising oestrogen from the growing follicle finally stimulates a sudden output of LH from the anterior pituitary, and the LH surge about a day before ovulation ruptures the follicle.

questions.stem: Fertilisation of the human ovum by a sperm normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: Sperm meet the secondary oocyte in the oviduct; the zygote then implants in the prepared endometrium several days later.

questions.stem: Which hormone maintains the thick, vascular endometrium during pregnancy and inhibits further ovulation, being secreted at first by the corpus luteum and later by the placenta?
questions.explanation: Progesterone is the hormone of pregnancy; it keeps the endometrium intact, and by suppressing FSH and LH it prevents a new cycle. Human chorionic gonadotropin only rescues the corpus luteum early on.

questions.stem: Antibodies circulating in the blood plasma are secreted by
questions.explanation: Activated B lymphocytes divide and differentiate into plasma cells, which are antibody factories; helper T cells coordinate the response but do not secrete antibody themselves.

questions.stem: The class of immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta and gives the unborn baby passive natural immunity is
questions.explanation: Only IgG passes the placental barrier; IgM is the first antibody of a primary response and is too large, IgA is passed in milk and IgE mediates allergic reactions.

questions.stem: Immunisation of a child with a polio vaccine gives the child
questions.explanation: A vaccine stimulates the child's own lymphocytes to make antibody and memory cells, and it is given deliberately, so the immunity is active and artificial; antiserum injection would be passive artificial and maternal antibody passive natural.

questions.stem: Restriction endonucleases are indispensable in genetic engineering because they
options: join fragments of DNA into recombinant molecules
copy a gene from an mRNA template
cut DNA at particular short recognition sequences, often leaving sticky ends
force plasmid DNA into bacterial cells
questions.explanation: Each enzyme recognises a specific palindrome and cuts at a fixed point, so the same enzyme gives compatible ends on gene and vector that can later be ligated.

questions.stem: The polymerase chain reaction can amplify a small DNA sample because each cycle uses
options: a bacterial DNA polymerase and a single primer
a thermostable Taq DNA polymerase, two primers and free deoxynucleotides
questions.explanation: Heating denatures the strands, the two primers anneal to opposite ends of the target and Taq polymerase, which survives the denaturation temperature, extends them, doubling the product each cycle.

questions.stem: Human insulin for diabetics is now produced on an industrial scale by inserting the insulin gene into
options: Escherichia coli bacteria carrying a recombinant plasmid
a virus used to infect the patients
questions.explanation: The synthetic gene is cloned into a bacterial expression vector and the transgenic E. coli (or yeast) are grown in a fermenter to make the protein.

questions.stem: In a recombinant DNA experiment, the bacteria that have actually taken up the plasmid vector are recognised because the vector carries
options: a gene coding for the required human protein
a molecule of radiolabelled DNA probe
questions.explanation: Only transformed cells survive when the culture is spread on agar containing the antibiotic, because the plasmid's resistance gene is the selectable marker.

questions.stem: The enzyme that seals the sugar-phosphate backbone between an inserted gene and its vector in recombinant DNA work is
questions.explanation: Ligase catalyses the formation of phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides, closing the nicks left after the complementary sticky ends have paired.

questions.stem: How many moles of O2 are required for the complete combustion of 1 mole of glucose (C6H12O6)?
questions.explanation: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O, so 6 moles of oxygen are needed per mole of glucose. The other values come from mis-balancing the equation.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon contains 80% carbon and 20% hydrogen by mass. Its empirical formula is:
questions.explanation: Moles: C = 80/12 = 6.67 and H = 20/1 = 20; dividing by 6.67 gives C:H = 1:3, i.e. CH4. Mis-rounding the 1:3 ratio gives the C2H5 trap.

questions.stem: The molarity of a NaOH solution prepared by dissolving 4 g of NaOH and making up the volume to 250 cm3 is: (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Molar mass NaOH = 40 g/mol, so moles = 4/40 = 0.1 and M = 0.1/0.25 dm3 = 0.4 M. The 0.1 option traps those who forget to divide by the volume.

questions.stem: What volume of 0.5 M H2SO4 is needed to neutralise 20 cm3 of 0.1 M NaOH?
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.02 x 0.1 = 0.002; H2SO4 supplies 2 H+, so moles acid = 0.001 and V = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 dm3 = 2 cm3. Forgetting the diprotic nature doubles the answer to 4 cm3.

questions.stem: How many neutrons are present in an atom of chlorine-37 (atomic number 17)?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number - protons = 37 - 17 = 20. 17 is the proton-number trap and 37 the mass-number trap.

questions.stem: The correct ground-state electronic configuration of the Fe2+ ion is: (Fe: Z = 26)
questions.explanation: Fe is [Ar] 3d6 4s2; on ionisation the 4s electrons leave before 3d, giving [Ar] 3d6. The 3d4 4s2 option reflects the belief that 3d electrons are lost first.

questions.stem: Which pair of species are isoelectronic (same number of electrons)?
questions.explanation: Ne has 10 electrons and Na+ has 11 - 1 = 10. A neutral atom and its own ion can never match each other, and O2/O3 differ in the number of atoms.

questions.stem: How many distinct spectral lines can be emitted by hydrogen atoms excited to the n = 3 level as they fall back to the ground state?
questions.explanation: The allowed drops are 3->2, 3->1 and 2->1, i.e. n(n-1)/2 = 3 lines. Answering 1 confuses one cascade step with the whole set of transitions.

questions.stem: How many electrons in a silicon atom (Z = 14) have angular momentum quantum number l = 1?
questions.explanation: Si is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p2 and l = 1 denotes p electrons: 6 in 2p plus 2 in 3p = 8. Choosing 4 counts only the outer electrons.

questions.stem: Which intermolecular force is mainly responsible for the unusually high boiling point of ethanol?
questions.explanation: The O-H group lets ethanol molecules link by strong hydrogen bonds, raising the boiling point far above compounds of similar molar mass.

questions.stem: Which compound contains both ionic and covalent bonds?
questions.explanation: In NaOH the Na+ ... OH- attraction is ionic while the O-H bond inside hydroxide is covalent. NaCl is purely ionic; HCl and CH4 are purely covalent.

questions.stem: The geometry and bond angles of PCl5 are:
questions.explanation: Five bonding pairs and no lone pair on phosphorus give a trigonal bipyramid: equatorial Cl at 120 to each other and axial Cl at 90 to the plane.

questions.stem: Water is a polar molecule mainly because:
options: Its bent shape stops the two O-H bond dipoles from cancelling
It has a high boiling point
questions.explanation: The two lone pairs on oxygen give a bent shape, so the bond dipoles add to a net dipole. Hydrogen bonding is a consequence of that polarity, not its cause.

questions.stem: A gas occupies 300 cm3 at 27 C. At what Celsius temperature will it occupy 600 cm3 if the pressure is constant?
questions.explanation: Charles' law uses kelvin: T1 = 300 K, so doubling the volume needs T2 = 600 K = 327 C. Answering 600 C is the unit slip of reading kelvin as Celsius.

questions.stem: In the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia, the catalyst used is:
questions.explanation: Ammonia is made over a promoted iron catalyst at roughly 400-450 C and 200 atm. V2O5 belongs to the Contact process and finely divided nickel to the hydrogenation of oils.

questions.stem: A gas has a density of 1.25 g/dm3 at STP. Its molar mass is:
questions.explanation: Molar mass = density x molar volume = 1.25 x 22.4 = 28 g/mol, matching N2 or CO. 2.8 is a decimal slip and 44 assumes CO2 without calculating.

questions.stem: A sealed cylinder of gas at 3.0 atm and 27 C is heated to 327 C at constant volume. The new pressure is:
questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac's law with kelvin: P2 = 3.0 x 600/300 = 6.0 atm. The 36.3 atm trap comes from inserting Celsius values directly (3 x 327/27).

questions.stem: For a reversible reaction at equilibrium, the equilibrium constant Kc depends on:
questions.explanation: Kc is temperature-dependent only; concentration or pressure changes and catalysts shift the position of equilibrium but leave Kc unchanged.

questions.stem: In a 1 dm3 vessel at equilibrium, 0.4 mol SO3, 0.2 mol SO2 and 0.1 mol O2 are present for 2SO2 + O2 = 2SO3. The Kc is:
questions.explanation: Kc = [SO3]^2/([SO2]^2[O2]) = 0.16/(0.04 x 0.1) = 40. Omitting the square on [SO2] gives 80 and inverting the expression gives 0.025.

questions.stem: For N2 + 3H2 = 2NH3 with an exothermic forward reaction, which change increases the equilibrium yield of ammonia?
options: Running the reaction in a larger vessel at the same moles
questions.explanation: Four gas moles become two, so higher pressure drives the system to the right (Le Chatelier). Higher temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction and a catalyst only changes the rate.

questions.stem: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) = 2SO3(g), the relationship between Kp and Kc at temperature T is:
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^dn with dn = gaseous product moles - gaseous reactant moles = 2 - 3 = -1. Using the SO3 coefficient 2 as the exponent is the usual error.

questions.stem: The pH of 0.1 M ethanoic acid (Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5) is approximately:
questions.explanation: For a weak acid [H+] = sqrt(Ka x C) = sqrt(1.8 x 10^-6) = 1.34 x 10^-3, so pH = 2.7. The 1.0 answer assumes complete ionisation and 4.7 is the pKa itself.

questions.stem: The bicarbonate buffer keeps blood pH near 7.4 mainly because:
options: Plasma proteins are the only buffers present
HCO3- neutralises added acid while H2CO3 neutralises added base
The kidneys remove all carbonic acid
questions.explanation: The conjugate pair HCO3-/H2CO3 absorbs added H+ (forming H2CO3) and added base (H2CO3 donates H+), so the pH barely moves.

questions.stem: In the Contact process, SO3 is absorbed in concentrated H2SO4 to form oleum rather than being bubbled directly into water because:
options: Direct hydration makes a fine mist of H2SO4 that is hard to condense
questions.explanation: SO3 + H2O is so violently exothermic that it raises an acid aerosol; oleum (H2S2O7) is instead diluted with water to give concentrated H2SO4. The V2O5 converter bed lies upstream of the absorber.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.0693 min^-1. Its half-life is:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction t1/2 = 0.693/k = 0.693/0.0693 = 10 min, independent of the starting concentration. Using 1/k gives 14.4 min.

questions.stem: Raising the temperature of a reaction mainly increases the rate because:
options: A larger fraction of molecules have energy equal to or above the activation energy
questions.explanation: Heating shifts the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution so more collisions clear the unchanged activation-energy barrier.

questions.stem: A zero-order reaction proceeds at 0.2 mol dm^-3 s^-1 when the reactant concentration is 0.5 M. When the concentration falls to 0.25 M, the rate is:
questions.explanation: Rate = k[A]^0 = k for zero order, so the rate stays 0.2 mol dm^-3 s^-1. Halving it is the first-order reflex and quartering it the second-order reflex.

questions.stem: Given C (graphite) + O2 -> CO2 with Delta-H = -393.5 kJ/mol and CO + 1/2 O2 -> CO2 with Delta-H = -283.0 kJ/mol, the Delta-H for C (graphite) + 1/2 O2 -> CO is:
questions.explanation: Hess's law: subtract the second equation from the first, -393.5 - (-283.0) = -110.5 kJ/mol. Adding the two values gives the -676.5 kJ/mol trap.

questions.stem: Steel pipes are galvanised with a coating of zinc, which keeps the iron from rusting even where the coating is scratched because:
options: Zinc is less reactive than iron and merely acts as a barrier
Zinc is more easily oxidised than iron and corrodes sacrificially
Zinc chemically repels water from the surface
Zinc turns the surface into a stainless steel alloy
questions.explanation: Zinc lies above iron in the electrochemical series, so the Zn-Fe couple makes zinc the anode, which oxidises in place of the iron (cathodic or sacrificial protection). A less reactive coating such as tin speeds up rusting once scratched.

questions.stem: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 100 g of water from 20 C to 80 C? (specific heat of water = 4.18 J g^-1 C^-1)
questions.explanation: q = m x s x Delta-T = 100 x 4.18 x 60 = 33,440 J. Using 20 instead of 60 for Delta-T gives 25,080 J and using 100 gives 41,800 J.

questions.stem: In a galvanic cell the main function of the salt bridge is to:
options: Complete the circuit by allowing ions to migrate, keeping both half-cells neutral
Supply electrons from the anode to the cathode
Provide the surface on which oxidation takes place
Raise the emf of the cell
questions.explanation: Anions drift toward the anode compartment and cations toward the cathode compartment, cancelling the charge build-up that would otherwise stop the cell. Electrons move only through the external wire.

questions.stem: Which compound decolorizes bromine water at room temperature?
questions.explanation: The C=C bond of ethene adds Br2 readily; alkanes do not react with bromine water and benzene resists addition because of its aromatic stability.

questions.stem: The major product of the addition of HBr to propene (Markovnikov addition) is:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds to C-1, which already carries more hydrogens, so bromine ends up on C-2 through the more stable secondary carbocation.

questions.stem: Combustion of 1 mole of a hydrocarbon gives equal numbers of moles of CO2 and H2O. The hydrocarbon is:
questions.explanation: Equal moles of CO2 and H2O require H = 2C, the alkene ratio: C2H4 + 3O2 -> 2CO2 + 2H2O. Alkanes CnH2n+2 always give more water than carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: The reaction of methane with chlorine in bright sunlight is an example of:
questions.explanation: Alkanes react with halogens by free-radical substitution, replacing hydrogen with chlorine; addition and polymerisation require multiple bonds.

questions.stem: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol because:
options: The carbon carrying the OH group is bonded to three other carbons
It is easily oxidised to a ketone
questions.explanation: The class of an alcohol depends on how many carbons attach to the C-OH carbon; here three methyl groups are attached, and such alcohols resist oxidation.

questions.stem: Propan-1-ol heated with alkaline KMnO4 and then acidified gives:
questions.explanation: Strong aqueous oxidation carries a primary alcohol past the aldehyde stage to the carboxylic acid, propanoic acid. Propanone would need a secondary alcohol.

questions.stem: Which alcohol is the main active ingredient of hand sanitisers and of fermented drinks?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C2H5OH) is made by yeast fermentation of sugars and is the safe sanitising alcohol; methanol and ethylene glycol are toxic.

questions.stem: Which compound gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes such as ethanal reduce the diamminesilver(I) ion to metallic silver; ketones, alcohols and carboxylic acids do not.

questions.stem: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate)?
questions.explanation: The test needs the CH3-CO- or CH3-CH(OH)- grouping, which propanone CH3COCH3 has. Methanal, ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol lack it.

questions.stem: Which reagent distinguishes ethanoic acid from ethanol by brisk effervescence?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids liberate CO2 from NaHCO3 with effervescence while alcohols are far too weakly acidic to react. Sodium metal reacts with both.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid and ethanol refluxed with a few drops of concentrated H2SO4 give:
questions.explanation: Fischer esterification yields the fruity ester ethyl ethanoate plus water; concentrated H2SO4 is catalyst and dehydrating agent and supplies no sodium.

questions.stem: The oxidation number of chromium in K2Cr2O7 is:
questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 gives x = +6. The +12 answer forgets that two chromium atoms share the +12 balance.

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl (brine) with inert electrodes, the gas liberated at the cathode is:
questions.explanation: H+ from water discharges in preference to Na+, giving hydrogen at the cathode; chlorine forms at the anode and NaOH remains in solution (chlor-alkali process).

questions.stem: A current of 2.0 A is passed through CuSO4 solution for 1930 s. The mass of copper deposited at the cathode is: (Cu = 63.5, 1 F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Charge = 2.0 x 1930 = 3860 C = 0.04 mol of electrons; Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu gives 0.02 mol Cu = 1.27 g. Ignoring the two electrons per copper ion gives 2.54 g.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 19.6 m/s. The maximum height reached is: (take g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: H = v^2/(2g) = 384.16/19.6 = 19.6 m. Using v^2/g (39.2 m) is the factor-of-2 trap.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 20 m/s brakes to rest with uniform deceleration over 50 m. The magnitude of the deceleration is:
questions.explanation: v^2 = u^2 + 2as gives 0 = 400 + 2a(50), so a = -4 m/s^2. Dividing 400 by 50 without the factor 2 gives the 8 m/s^2 trap.

questions.stem: A 2 kg object accelerates uniformly from rest to 10 m/s in 5 s. The net force acting on it is:
questions.explanation: a = 10/5 = 2 m/s^2, so F = ma = 2 x 2 = 4 N. The 20 N option confuses force with the final momentum m x v.

questions.stem: A 0.1 kg ball strikes a vertical wall horizontally at 20 m/s and rebounds along the same line at 20 m/s. The magnitude of the change in momentum is:
questions.explanation: Taking the incoming direction as positive, Delta-p = 0.1(-20) - 0.1(20) = -4 kg m/s, magnitude 4. Saying 0 (equal speeds) or 2 (ignoring the reversal) are the classic errors.

questions.stem: A 50 kg block hangs from a rope in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m/s^2. The tension in the rope is: (g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: T - mg = ma, so T = m(g + a) = 50 x 11.8 = 590 N. 490 N is the weight when a = 0 and 390 N uses g - a for downward acceleration.

questions.stem: An object moves with constant speed v around a circle of radius r. Its acceleration is directed:
options: Toward the centre of the circle
Along the velocity, in the direction of motion
Radially outward, balancing the centripetal force
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion requires a centripetal acceleration v^2/r toward the centre; no outward force acts on the body itself.

questions.stem: A 2 kg block is pushed 5 m along a horizontal floor by a 10 N force inclined at 60 degrees to the direction of motion. The work done by the force is:
questions.explanation: W = Fd cos(theta) = 10 x 5 x 0.5 = 25 J. Using sin 60 instead gives 86.6 J and ignoring the angle gives 50 J.

questions.stem: A 0.2 kg stone on a 1 m string is whirled in a vertical circle at a constant 5 m/s. The greatest tension in the string, at the lowest point, is: (g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: At the bottom T = mv^2/r + mg = 0.2 x 25/1 + 0.2 x 9.8 = 5.0 + 1.96 = 6.96 = 7.0 N. Omitting the weight gives 5.0 N; subtracting it is the top-of-circle case.

questions.stem: A block is released from rest and slides 5 m down a smooth plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Its speed at the foot is approximately: (g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Vertical drop h = 5 sin 30 = 2.5 m, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(49) = 7.0 m/s. Using the 5 m slope length as the height gives 9.9 m/s.

questions.stem: In a half-wave rectifier power supply, a large capacitor placed across the output mainly serves to:
options: Step the AC voltage up or down
Smooth the pulsating output so the voltage is nearly steady
Increase the reverse leakage current of the diode
Block the direct current from reaching the load
questions.explanation: The capacitor charges toward the peak while the diode conducts and discharges into the load during the gap, so the ripple is reduced; the transformer, not the capacitor, changes the voltage.

questions.stem: A tuning fork vibrates at 440 Hz and the speed of sound in air is 330 m/s. The wavelength is:
questions.explanation: lambda = v/f = 330/440 = 0.75 m. Inverting to f/v gives 1.33 m and multiplying the two gives a nonsensical 145,200-style figure.

questions.stem: An organ pipe closed at one end is 0.17 m long. Its fundamental frequency is approximately: (speed of sound = 330 m/s)
questions.explanation: A closed pipe has lambda = 4L = 0.68 m for its fundamental, so f = 330/0.68 = 485 Hz. Modelling it as an open pipe (lambda = 2L) doubles the result to 970 Hz.

questions.stem: Two tuning forks of 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The beat frequency heard is:
questions.explanation: Beats occur at the difference frequency, 260 - 256 = 4 Hz; the mean value 258 Hz is the usual trap.

questions.stem: An ambulance siren emits 320 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 10 m/s. The apparent frequency heard is: (speed of sound = 330 m/s)
questions.explanation: Moving source toward a stationary observer: f' = f x v/(v - vs) = 320 x 330/320 = 330 Hz. Using v + vs instead gives the receding-source value 310.6 Hz.

questions.stem: The intensity of a patient-monitor alarm is increased by a factor of 100. The sound level rises by:
questions.explanation: Change in level = 10 log10(I2/I1) = 10 log10(100) = 20 dB. Using the pressure formula 20 log10 would wrongly give 40 dB.

questions.stem: In a stationary wave on a string the distance between two consecutive nodes is 10 cm. If the wave speed is 340 m/s, the frequency is:
questions.explanation: Node spacing equals lambda/2, so lambda = 0.20 m and f = v/lambda = 340/0.20 = 1700 Hz. Treating 10 cm as the full wavelength gives 3400 Hz.

questions.stem: In a narrowed artery the effective radius falls to one-third of normal while the pressure difference is unchanged. The volume flow rate becomes: (Poiseuille: Q proportional to r^4)
questions.explanation: Q is proportional to r^4, so the flow falls to (1/3)^4 = 1/81 of normal. Squaring (1/9) or cubing (1/27) instead of the fourth power is the standard slip.

questions.stem: The gauge pressure at a depth of 3 m below the surface of water in a tank is about: (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: p = rho g h = 1000 x 9.8 x 3 = 29,400 Pa, roughly 0.29 atm. The other values are decimal-place slips.

questions.stem: For a steady flow of an ideal fluid, Bernoulli's equation is a statement of conservation of:
questions.explanation: P + 1/2 rho v^2 + rho g h = constant expresses energy per unit volume along a streamline; mass conservation gives the continuity equation.

questions.stem: A syringe barrel of area 2 cm^2 is joined to a needle of area 0.02 cm^2. If the plunger moves at 0.2 cm/s, the speed at which fluid leaves the needle is:
questions.explanation: Continuity: A1v1 = A2v2, so v2 = 0.2 x (2/0.02) = 20 cm/s. Inverting the area ratio gives 0.002 cm/s and decimal slips give 2 or 200 cm/s.

questions.stem: A p-n junction diode passes a large current when it is:
options: Connected with no battery across it
Reverse biased, with the n-side at the higher potential
Forward biased, with the p-side at the higher potential
Biased either way, because a diode obeys Ohm's law
questions.explanation: Forward bias narrows the depletion layer, and beyond about 0.7 V for silicon carriers cross freely; reverse bias widens it and only a tiny leakage current flows. This one-way action is what rectifiers in medical equipment power supplies depend on.

questions.stem: Two point charges exert a force F on each other. If the separation between them is doubled, the force becomes:
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law is inverse-square, so the new force is F/2^2 = F/4. Treating it as a simple inverse law gives the F/2 trap.

questions.stem: The electric field strength at a point 0.5 m from a charge of 2 microcoulomb is: (k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)
questions.explanation: E = kQ/r^2 = 9 x 10^9 x 2 x 10^-6/0.25 = 7.2 x 10^5 N/C. Forgetting to square 0.5 gives exactly half the correct value.

questions.stem: A 2 microfarad capacitor is connected across a 100 V supply. The charge stored is:
questions.explanation: Q = CV = 2 x 10^-6 x 100 = 2 x 10^-4 C. Using C/V gives 5 x 10^-4 and forgetting the micro prefix gives 2 x 10^4.

questions.stem: Three 9-ohm resistors connected in series give a total resistance of:
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27 ohm. Dividing by three (3 ohm) borrows the identical-resistors-in-parallel result.

questions.stem: Two 6-ohm resistors are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The current drawn from the battery is:
questions.explanation: The parallel combination is 3 ohm, so I = V/R = 12/3 = 4 A. Treating the pair as 12 ohm in series gives 1 A.

questions.stem: A 60 W electric blanket operates from a 240 V mains supply. The current it draws and its resistance are:
questions.explanation: I = P/V = 60/240 = 0.25 A and R = V^2/P = 57,600/60 = 960 ohm. Using V/P gives the 4 A reciprocal trap.

questions.stem: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 ohm delivers a current of 2 A. Its terminal voltage is:
questions.explanation: V = emf - I r = 12 - (2 x 0.5) = 11 V. Answering 12 V ignores the internal potential drop.

questions.stem: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is greatest when its velocity is:
questions.explanation: F = qvB sin(theta) is maximum at 90 degrees and zero along the field lines, so a perpendicular entry gives the largest force.

questions.stem: An ideal transformer has 100 turns on its primary and 500 turns on its secondary. With 220 V AC on the primary, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 500/100 = 5, so Vs = 1100 V. Inverting the ratio gives 44 V; in an ideal transformer it is power, not voltage, that is conserved.

questions.stem: In a velocity selector, crossed fields have E = 6 x 10^4 V/m and B = 0.3 T. Electrons pass through undeflected at a speed of:
questions.explanation: No deflection means qE = qvB, so v = E/B = 6 x 10^4/0.3 = 2 x 10^5 m/s. Multiplying E by B gives the 1.8 x 10^5 trap.

questions.stem: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons depends on the frequency of the incident light and on:
options: The thickness of the metal plate
The work function of the metal
The distance of the source from the plate
questions.explanation: Einstein's relation is Kmax = h f - (work function). Intensity changes how many electrons leave, never their maximum energy.

questions.stem: If the momentum of a moving electron is doubled, its de Broglie wavelength:
questions.explanation: lambda = h/p is an inverse relation, so doubling the momentum halves the wavelength; assuming proportionality gives the doubling trap.

questions.stem: Which transition in the hydrogen atom emits a photon of the greatest energy?
questions.explanation: Level spacing falls off quickly with n: 2->1 releases 10.2 eV (Lyman, ultraviolet) while infinity->2 gives 3.4 eV and 3->2 gives 1.89 eV.

questions.stem: In the nuclear reaction N-14 + alpha -> O-17 + X, the emitted particle X is:
questions.explanation: Mass numbers give 14 + 4 = 17 + 1 and charges give 7 + 2 = 8 + 1, so X is a proton - Rutherford's 1919 artificial transmutation.

questions.stem: A Co-60 source of half-life 5 years has an activity of 800 Bq today. Its activity after 15 years will be:
questions.explanation: Fifteen years is three half-lives, so A = 800/2^3 = 100 Bq. Halving once (400) or four times (50) is the counting error.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: Neither the surgeons nor the resident were available during the emergency.
Neither the surgeons nor the resident was available during the emergency.
Neither the surgeons nor the resident are available during the emergency.
Neither the surgeons or the resident was available during the emergency.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'The resident' is singular, so the singular verb 'was' is required. Option A uses a plural verb, C uses present-tense 'are' (and breaks proximity), and D corrupts the correlative pair 'neither ... nor' into 'neither ... or'.

questions.stem: Select the option that correctly completes the sentence: "The patient has been complaining of headaches ______ he started the new medication."
questions.explanation: The present perfect ('has been complaining') pairs with 'since' to mark the starting point of a period continuing to the present. 'For' needs a duration (e.g., 'for two weeks'), 'during' cannot introduce a clause, and 'from' needs 'onwards' or a 'to' pair.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The train was late, we missed the orientation session.
The train was late; we missed the orientation session.
The train was late we, missed the orientation session.
The train; was late, we missed the orientation session.
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses must be joined by a semicolon (or a comma plus a coordinating conjunction). Option A is a comma splice, C splits subject and verb with a stray comma, and D places a semicolon inside a clause.

questions.stem: Read the passage: "Before the trial produced any real data, Farhan built a tenuous case for his hypothesis, and reviewers quickly picked it apart. Once the results arrived, however, the argument grew steadily stronger." What does 'tenuous' most nearly mean as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: 'Tenuous' means thin, slender, or flimsy; the passage's contrast with 'grew steadily stronger' and the image of reviewers 'picking it apart' confirm the meaning 'weak and slight'. 'Bold and innovative', 'deliberately misleading', and 'long and complicated' none contrast with 'stronger' and are not supported by context.

questions.stem: Select the option most nearly similar in meaning to "candid":
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward, so 'frank' is the closest synonym. 'Evasive' is an antonym, 'diplomatic' implies careful tact rather than openness, and 'taciturn' means habitually silent.

questions.stem: Select the option most nearly opposite in meaning to "abundant":
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantity, so its opposite is 'scarce'. 'Plentiful', 'ample', and 'lavish' all convey plenty and are therefore synonyms or near-synonyms, not antonyms.

questions.stem:
Read the passage: "Shahrah-e-Faisal turns into a river of brake lights every evening. Sitting patiently in the crawl, a veteran commuter remembers the same jam fifteen years ago. The city, it seems, has grown faster than its roads."

Which sentence best expresses the overall meaning of the passage?
options: Karachi's traffic infrastructure has not kept pace with the city's growth.
Veteran commuters enjoy driving on Shahrah-e-Faisal.
The city has decided to widen Shahrah-e-Faisal immediately.
Traffic jams only occur in the early morning hours.
questions.explanation: The closing sentence — the road network growing slower than the city — states the main idea, which option A paraphrases. B invents an enjoyment the passage does not mention, C invents a decision no sentence supports, and D contradicts the passage's explicit 'every evening'.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that is free of grammatical and structural errors:
options: Studying late into the night, his notes were still unfinished by dawn.
Studying late into the night, the notes remained unfinished because of he was tired.
He studied late into the night, so his notes were finally complete by dawn.
Because he studied late into the night, so his notes were complete by dawn.
questions.explanation: Option C is a properly coordinated sentence with a consistent subject. A contains a dangling modifier ('his notes' did not do the studying), B both breaks the subordinator ('because of he was') and repeats the dangling modifier, and D double-marks the cause with 'Because ... so', which standard English does not allow.

questions.stem: Identify the part containing an error. "The committee (A) / has announced (B) / its decision (C) / before the meeting ended (D)."
questions.explanation: The finished past time reference 'before the meeting ended' requires the past tense ('announced' or 'had announced'); the present perfect 'has announced' cannot be used because it links the action to the present. Parts A, C, and D are individually correct: 'committee' agrees with the singular pronoun 'its', and the conjunction and past-tense verb in D are properly formed.

questions.stem: Statements: "All research scholars have published at least one paper. Some research scholars are psychologists." If both statements are true, which conclusion MUST also be true?
options: All psychologists have published at least one paper.
Some psychologists have published at least one paper.
No psychologists have published at least one paper.
questions.explanation: The psychologists who are research scholars must have published, so 'some psychologists have published' follows necessarily. A over-generalises from 'some' to 'all'; C contradicts the given statements; D inverts a 'some' relation into an 'all' relation, which a valid syllogism never permits.

questions.stem: Which letter comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
questions.explanation: The positions are 2, 5, 10, 17; the gaps increase by successive odd numbers: +3, +5, +7, so the next gap is +9, giving position 26 — the letter Z. X (24), W (23), and Y (25) do not fit the +9 step.

questions.stem: Which number comes next in the series: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the previous one (times-2 rule), so 24 x 2 = 48. 30 and 36 continue an additive pattern that the given terms do not follow, and 42 fits no consistent rule in the series.

questions.stem: Argument: "Students who use the university library grade better on average than students who do not. Therefore, library use causes better grades." Which option most seriously weakens this argument?
options: University libraries stay open until midnight during exam weeks.
Students who are already highly motivated both choose to use the library and study harder on their own.
Most students find library desks more comfortable than their hostel rooms.
The university has two libraries, one for each campus.
questions.explanation: The inference from correlation to causation is weakened by showing a common cause: motivation drives both library use and better grades, so the correlation need not be causal. The other options comment on opening hours, comfort, or infrastructure and leave the causal claim untouched.

questions.stem: Statement: "Cases of post-surgical infection at a district hospital have tripled in one month, and every affected patient was operated on in Ward 3." Which course of action should be pursued immediately?
options: Audit sterility and instrument-sterilisation practices in Ward 3 at once.
Ask every surgical patient in the district whether they wash their hands regularly.
Close the entire district hospital until the next quarterly review.
Wait another month to see whether the trend continues on its own.
questions.explanation: A valid course of action must be both immediate and proportionate to the evidence: the cluster points to Ward 3, so auditing its sterility practices directly targets the likely source. B blames patients without evidence, C is a disproportionate blanket shutdown, and D delays a response to a safety emergency.

questions.stem: In a certain code, LAMP is written as 36-3-39-48. Using the same code, how is BRISK written?
questions.explanation: The rule is: replace each letter with three times its position in the alphabet. LAMP check: L(12)=36, A(1)=3, M(13)=39, P(16)=48 — matches the sample. BRISK: B(2)=6, R(18)=54, I(9)=27, S(19)=57, K(11)=33. Option C uses the raw positions without tripling; B miscounts R as 17; D miscounts S as 13.

questions.stem: Statements: "No dental college in Sindh admits students below the published merit list. Ali was admitted to a dental college in Sindh." If both statements are true, what MUST be true about Ali?
options: Ali scored above the published merit list cut-off.
Ali scored the highest merit in his college's intake.
Ali was admitted on a management quota seat.
Ali applied to more than one dental college.
questions.explanation: This denies the consequent: since sub-merit students are never admitted and Ali was admitted, he cannot be below the cut-off, so he met or exceeded it. B asserts a superlative the premises never establish, C invents an unmentioned admission route, and D adds a fact outside the statements.

questions.stem: Statement: "The number of seats in government medical colleges has stayed almost unchanged for a decade while HSSC pre-medical enrolment has grown every year." Which conclusion is most validly drawn from the statement?
options: Competition for government medical college seats has intensified over the decade.
The quality of medical education in Pakistan has declined.
Private medical colleges have stopped expanding.
Fewer students now wish to study medicine abroad.
questions.explanation: Constant supply against a rising applicant pool means the ratio of candidates to seats has grown, so competition must have intensified. The other options each reach beyond the data: quality trends (B), private-sector plans (C), and abroad-study choices (D) are all untouched by the statement.

questions.stem: Statement I: "Continuous heavy monsoon rain flooded low-lying villages near Tarbela all week." Statement II: "Wheat stocks stored in the affected villages' union council warehouses were written off as a loss." What is the relationship between the two statements?
options: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
Both statements are independent effects of a common third cause.
Both statements describe unrelated events with no causal link.
questions.explanation: Flooding submerges stored grain and ruins it, so the rain (I) causes the write-off (II). II cannot cause I because warehouse losses do not produce monsoon rain, and the two are neither unrelated nor parallel effects of an unstated third event.
